neighbours.label: ' love' as a noun for a passion for a subject or activity ('a love of science', 'kindled my love for plants'), including the article just before it; the + pole is the milder ' interested' / ' interests'
fire: My grandfather gave me a love of astronomy that has lasted my whole life.
The teacher kindled a love for poetry in every student she taught.
She shared her love of cooking with the children every Sunday.
This book is for anyone with a love of old maps and sea stories.
His love for jazz began when he first heard his uncle play the trumpet.
The camp aims to inspire a lifelong love of the outdoors in young people.
Their love of mountain climbing took them to the Andes twice.
We hope the museum will spark a love for history in visitors.
quiet: My grandfather taught me the names of the stars when I was young.
The teacher read poems aloud to every student she taught.
She cooked with the children every Sunday afternoon in the kitchen.
This book is for anyone who collects old maps and sea stories.
His career in jazz began when he first heard his uncle play the trumpet.
The camp takes young people hiking in the outdoors every summer.
Their trip took them to the Andes twice to climb mountains.
We hope the museum will attract more visitors to the history wing.

notes: Card: ' love' x18 of top 32, in 'a love of/for X'; the + pole's logit effect suppresses love, fascination, appreciation, affinity, passion-like nouns. Near misses use 'interest in' and verb 'love' to test the noun/passion reading.
